title: He said he was the weakest…
paragraphs:
He said he was the weakest…
—and heaven didn’t argue.

Because most of us are waiting for God to disagree with our insecurity.
To correct it.
To comfort it.
But in Judges 6, God does something unsettling.

He calls a weak man…
while letting him feel weak.
Gideon is not standing on a battlefield.

Threshing wheat in a winepress—
a cramped, hollow pit meant for crushing grapes, not harvesting grain.

The Midianites had stripped Israel bare.
Raided their food.
Burned their land.
Left them surviving in caves like fugitives.

Stay small.
Stay unseen.
Stay safe.
Until one sentence shattered his hiding place:
“The Lord is with you, mighty warrior.” (Judges 6:12)
Nothing in Gideon’s life matched that word.

No victories.
No reputation.
No confidence.
So he pushes back—honest, raw, almost offensive:
“My clan is the weakest… and I am the least in my family.” (Judges 6:15)
And here’s where the story cuts into us.

Because Gideon didn’t just see himself as weak—
he had built his identity around it.

Weak became his name.
His narrative.
His excuse.

“I’m not ready.”
“I’m not enough.”
“I’m too broken.”
“I messed up too much.”

Those words feel true.
But they’re not final.
God doesn’t respond to Gideon with a motivational speech.
He doesn’t say, “No, you’re actually strong!”

Because the answer to your weakness…
is not a better version of you.
It’s the presence of God with you.

So when victory comes—
no one will confuse it with human ability.
This is the scandal of how God works.

He chooses the unlikely.
Uses the unqualified.
Empowers the insufficient.
But because He’s magnifying His grace.
As it is written in 2 Corinthians 12:9:
“My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is made perfect in weakness.”
Gideon’s story is not the end.
Because centuries later, another Deliverer would come…

Not riding in power—
but wrapped in humility.

Born in obscurity.
Rejected by His own.
Crucified like a criminal.

Sin lost its grip.
Death lost its sting.

And what looked like weakness…
became the greatest victory in history.

Gideon with 300 men.
Jesus on a cross.
Both moments whisper the same truth:
What have you been calling weakness?

Your past?
Your failure?
Your fear?
Your insecurity?
That’s the exact place God wants to meet you?
“Come as you are… and I will make you new.”

Even after the calling.
Even after the signs.
But obedience in the middle of it.
Stop arguing with God about your limitations.
Stop disqualifying yourself from the story He’s writing.
If He called Gideon in a pit…
If He saved the world through a cross…
What makes you think your weakness is too much?
You are not the exception to God’s grace.
You are the reason it exists.

Your insecurity.
Your shame.
Your “I’m not enough.”

Because the same God who called Gideon “mighty”
while he was still hiding—
Someone you know is still hiding in their winepress.

God still chooses the weakest—
and turns them into testimonies of His power.
